sections.title: Official rule
sections.body: LSE’s current Master of Public Policy page states: applicants must have at least five years of policy-relevant experience, although exceptions may be granted for outstanding candidates with slightly less experience. The same page describes the MPP as designed for mid-career professionals with more than five years’ experience. This is an eligibility/entry requirement, not merely a competitive preference. citeturn0search0

sections.title: Applicant’s experience
sections.body: Based on the supplied employment history, the Accra Metropolitan Research Unit role ran from 5 September 2022 to 15 December 2023, and the Institute for Fiscal Studies role from 4 March 2024 to the present. As of 8 August 2026, these total approximately 3 years 8 months of employment, excluding the documented 16 December 2023–3 March 2024 gap. Both roles are substantively policy-research roles: municipal revenue, social-protection targeting, quasi-experimental evaluation, and a policy brief on property-rate compliance. They should therefore be presented as policy-relevant experience, but they fall about 16 months short of five years.

sections.title: Eligibility versus competitiveness
sections.body: Conclusion: the roles do not, on the ordinary reading of LSE’s published rule, satisfy the five-year minimum yet. They may support an exception request because the applicant has strong, directly relevant quantitative policy work and a First Class economics degree, but LSE does not define the exception threshold or guarantee that this profile will qualify. LSE also reports that its MPP students average 10 years of work experience, which is contextual evidence of a competitive norm rather than a separate eligibility rule. citeturn0search0

sections.title: Recommended application treatment
sections.body: Do not state that the applicant meets the MPP’s five-year requirement. State the exact dates and describe the roles as approximately 3 years 8 months of policy-relevant experience as of 8 August 2026. If applying before reaching five years, explicitly frame the application around the published exception for outstanding candidates with slightly less experience and support it with the First Class degree, strong econometrics and statistics results, applied evaluation work, and policy impact evidence. This is an inference about positioning, not an LSE-confirmed exception decision.

follow_ups: Verify the exact submission date before applying, because the experience total will change and LSE’s rolling admissions status may change.
